abstractExcerpt: Architected materials achieve programmable mechanical behavior through spatially encoded compositional heterogeneity, yet inferring encoded stiffness fractions from structural appearance alone remains unreliable when mechanically distinct configurations are visually indistinguishable prior to loading. Here we show that deformation sequences acquired during tensile loading constitute a physically meaningful information channel for continuous design-space inference, and introduce a design-space digital twin, a single learned model spanning a continuous material design space.

Here we combined interpretable machine learning with targeted catalyst synthesis to identify and validate the descriptors controlling hydrocracking selectivity over Y zeolites.

abstractExcerpt: High-throughput materials discovery often begins with large sets of candidate compositions, while density functional theory (DFT), synthesis, and high-fidelity characterization remain expensive enough to require early prioritization. Accurately resolving the 3D atomic structure with sub-angstrom precision is thus essential for rational design. Here, we applied atomic electron tomography (AET) to determine, for the first time, the 3D atomic structure of complex core/shell QDs, resolving over 14,000 atoms per particle.
